auth.label: Application Password
auth.description: Pi-hole application password used to authenticate against the instance API. Use an application password, not your account password, because application passwords bypass two-factor authentication. Create one from your Pi-hole web interface under Settings -> All settings -> API.

extraFields.label: Instance Base URL
extraFields.description: The root URL for your Pi-hole instance, for example http://pi.hole or https://pi.hole:8443. The API is served below this root.

extraFields.label: API Path
extraFields.description: The URL path below the instance root where the Pi-hole API is served, normally api. Change this only when a reverse proxy rewrites the API to a different subpath.

actions.name: get_queries
actions.description: Query the Pi-hole DNS log with optional filters. By default returns the most recent queries; each response exposes a cursor for the next chunk.

from.description: Only return queries from this Unix timestamp onward.

until.description: Only return queries up to this Unix timestamp.

length.description: Maximum number of results to return.

cursor.description: Database ID of the most recent query to show; use the cursor of a previous response.

domain.description: Filter by queried domain, * wildcards supported.

clientIp.description: Filter by requesting client IP address, * wildcards supported.

clientName.description: Filter by requesting client hostname, * wildcards supported.

upstream.description: Filter by upstream destination (may also be cache, blocklist, or permitted), * wildcards supported.

type.description: Filter by query type, for example A or AAAA.

status.description: Filter by query status, for example GRAVITY or FORWARDED.

reply.description: Filter by reply type, for example NODATA or NXDOMAIN.

dnssec.description: Filter by DNSSEC status, for example SECURE or INSECURE.

disk.description: Read queries from the long-term on-disk database instead of the in-memory database.

inputSchema.description: Input parameters for querying the Pi-hole DNS log.

anyOf.description: Database ID of the most recent query shown, for the next chunk.

cursor.description: Database ID of the most recent query shown, for the next chunk.

recordsFiltered.description: Number of available queries after filtering.

anyOf.description: Earliest timestamp of queries held in the in-memory database (Unix time).

earliestTimestamp.description: Earliest timestamp of queries held in the in-memory database (Unix time).

anyOf.description: Earliest timestamp of queries held in the long-term on-disk database (Unix time).

earliestTimestampDisk.description: Earliest timestamp of queries held in the long-term on-disk database (Unix time).
